trial_name.text: Three multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies (referred to as Studies 1, 2, and 3 in the label); the pivotal trials in the reviewer's naming were studies 3065 A1-205, VRX-RET-E22-301, and VRX-RET-E22-302.

design.text: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; patients randomized to total daily maintenance dosages of 600, 900, or 1,200 mg/day administered in 3 equally divided doses, with titration from 300 mg/day.

citations.quote: The efficacy of POTIGA as adjunctive therapy in partial-onset seizures was established in 3 multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies in 1,239 adult patients.
Patients were randomized to the total daily maintenance dosages of 600 mg/day, 900 mg/day, or 1,200 mg/day, each administered in 3 equally divided doses.
During the titration phase of all 3 studies, treatment was initiated at 300 mg/day (100 mg 3 times per day) and increased in weekly increments of 150 mg/day to the target maintenance dosage.

population.text: Adult patients with partial-onset seizures with or without secondary generalization, not adequately controlled with 1 to 3 concomitant AEDs; mean duration of epilepsy 22 years; median baseline seizure frequency 8 to 12 seizures per month.

citations.quote: Patients enrolled in the studies had partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization and were not adequately controlled with 1 to 3 concomitant AEDs, with or without concomitant vagus nerve stimulation.
Patients had a mean duration of epilepsy of 22 years. Across the 3 studies, the median baseline seizure frequency ranged from 8 to 12 seizures per month.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was the percent change in seizure frequency from baseline in the double-blind treatment phase (criterion for statistical significance P<0.05).

citations.quote: The primary endpoint consisted of the percent change in seizure frequency from baseline in the double-blind treatment phase.
The criteria for statistical significance was P<0.05.
The efficacy of POTIGA as adjunctive therapy in partial-onset seizures was established in 3 multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies in 1,239 adult patients.

result.text: A statistically significant reduction in median percent 28-day seizure frequency versus placebo was observed with POTIGA at 600 mg/day (Study 1), 900 mg/day (Studies 1 and 3), and 1,200 mg/day (Studies 2 and 3).

citations.quote: Figure 1 shows the median percent reduction in 28-day seizure frequency (baseline to double-blind phase) as compared with placebo across all 3 studies. A statistically significant effect was observed with POTIGA at doses of 600 mg/day (Study 1), at 900 mg/day (Studies 1 and 3), and at 1,200 mg/day (Studies 2 and 3).

indication.text: POTIGA is indicated as adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients aged 18 years and older.

citations.quote: POTIGA™ is indicated as adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients aged 18 years and older.

target_moa.text: Ezogabine is a potassium channel opener; in vitro it enhances transmembrane potassium currents mediated by the KCNQ (Kv7.2 to 7.5) family of ion channels, thereby stabilizing the resting membrane potential and reducing brain excitability.

citations.quote: POTIGA is a potassium channel opener indicated as adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients aged 18 years and older. (1)

*In vitro* studies indicate that ezogabine enhances transmembrane potassium currents mediated by the KCNQ (Kv7.2 to 7.5) family of ion channels. By activating KCNQ channels, ezogabine is thought to stabilize the resting membrane potential and reduce brain excitability.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (vs placebo) were dose-related CNS/psychiatric effects: dizziness (23% overall; 32% at 1,200 mg/day vs 9% placebo), somnolence (22% vs 12% placebo), fatigue (15% overall), confusional state (16% at 1,200 mg/day vs 3% placebo), and tremor (8% overall); urinary retention was reported in approximately 2% (29 of 1,365) of patients and is a labeled warning.

detail.text: A REMS was required, consisting of a communication plan (Dear Health Care Practitioner letters describing the risk of urinary retention) and a timetable for submission of assessments.

citations.quote: Your proposed REMS, submitted on June 9, 2011, and appended to this letter, is approved. The REMS consists of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.
The REMS will consist of a communication plan that itself consists of Dear Health Care Practitioner letters describing the risk of urinary retention.

vote.text: The drug's potential to cause urinary symptoms, including urinary retention, was discussed at a Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems (PCNS) Advisory Committee meeting held on 8/11/10.

citations.quote: This action is presumably related to the pharmacology of ezogabine, and was fully discussed at a meeting of the Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems (PCNS) Advisory Committee held on 8/11/10.

detail.text: Not a first-cycle approval; FDA issued a Complete Response letter on 11/30/10, and approval followed the sponsor's Class 1 resubmission (complete response) of 4/15/11.

citations.quote: The Agency issued a Complete Response to the sponsor on 11/30/10; the primary reason for the CR action was stated as follows, taken verbatim from the CR letter:
The April 15, 2011, submission constituted a complete response to our November 30, 2010, action letter.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated October 30, 2009, received October 30, 2009, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Potiga (ezogabine) Tablets, 50mg, 200mg, 300mg, and 400 mg.

requirement.text: 1781-1: Conduct a prospective, randomized, placebo-control, double-blinded efficacy/safety trial of Potiga (ezogabine) in children >=12 years old (required pediatric assessment).

citations.quote: 1781-1 Conduct a prospective, randomized, placebo-control, double-blinded efficacy/safety trial of Potiga (ezogabine) in children \ge 12 years old.

requirement.text: 1781-2: Conduct a long-term open label extension study of ezogabine in children >=12 years old (required pediatric assessment).

citations.quote: 1781-2 Conduct a long-term open label extension study of ezogabine in children \ge 12 years old.

requirement.text: 1781-3: A prospective cohort study to better define the risk of urinary retention in patients with epilepsy treated with ezogabine, analyzing approximately 2,000 to 4,000 ezogabine-exposed patients.

citations.quote: 1781-3 A prospective cohort study to better define the risk of urinary retention in patients with epilepsy treated with ezogabine and how the risk may vary with demographics (e.g. age), comorbidities that influence voiding (e.g., benign prostatic hyperplasia [BPH], multiple sclerosis) and concomitant medications that may influence voiding. The study will be performed utilizing a research database to compare patients started in two cohorts, those started on ezogabine with those started on other anticonvulsants, for the incidence of urinary retention. The study will analyze approximately 2,000 to 4,000 ezogabine-exposed patients.

requirement.text: 1781-7: A controlled urodynamic trial, including adults of both sexes in a wide range of ages, with pre- and post-drug urodynamic measures (uroflowmetry, multichannel cystometry, EMG, subjective sensory reporting).

citations.quote: 1781-7 A controlled urodynamic trial, to include adults of both sexes in a wide range of ages, including the elderly. Pre- and post-drug urodynamic measures should be carefully collected. Urodynamic measurements should include, although not necessarily be limited to, uroflowmetry, multichannel cystometry, electromyography (EMG), and subjective sensory reporting.

citations.quote: The NDA is not approvable due to the high specification limit proposed for the mutagenic impurity (b) (4) was reproducibly positive in the Ames assay, both in the presence and absence of metabolic activation.

summary.text: Standard NDA 505(b) review. The original NDA (received 10/30/09) received a Complete Response on 11/30/10 for a CMC/nonclinical mutagenic-impurity deficiency; the sponsor submitted a Class 1 complete-response resubmission on 4/15/11, and the application was approved with a required REMS (communication plan) and multiple postmarketing requirements including pediatric and urinary-retention studies.
